items.description: Resolve a local time to an exact UTC instant with explicit DST ambiguity handling, business-day arithmetic, public-holiday status, and working-hour overlap across timezones. Detects ambiguous and nonexistent local times instead of silently shifting them. Declares its IANA tzdb release and per-jurisdiction holiday provenance.

add_business_days.description: Move this many working days from the resolved date, skipping the calendar's weekend days and its public holidays. Zero returns the date unchanged.

ambiguity_policy.description: How to read a local time that occurs twice or not at all. Matches Temporal's disambiguation vocabulary. The default, reject, returns verdict "unknown" with both candidate instants rather than silently picking one.

compare_with.description: Other IANA zones to report the same instant in, and to intersect working hours with.

holiday_calendar.description: Jurisdiction whose public holidays and weekend definition apply. An unlisted value is rejected with UNSUPPORTED; this service never falls back to an empty holiday list.

instant.description: An absolute ISO 8601 instant ending in Z or an explicit offset. Alternative to local_time; send exactly one of the two.

local_time.description: ISO local date and time with NO offset and no Z suffix. This is the field whose meaning can be ambiguous, which is the point of the endpoint.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier, resolved against tzdb 2026c.

working_hours.description: Local business hours, defaulting to 09:00-17:00. end < start means the window crosses midnight.

data_versions.description: Declares the pinned IANA tzdb release, holiday dataset, and Temporal source.

candidates.description: Both candidate instants when the local time is ambiguous or nonexistent.

verdict.description: unknown when the local time is ambiguous or nonexistent under a reject policy.

format.description: json: the whole result object. markdown: the markdown body alone, sent as text/markdown. Omit it and the format follows the Accept header (text/markdown → markdown), else json.

render.description: auto: static first, browser only when the page looks client-rendered. static: never use a browser. browser: always render in a headless browser.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL to convert; percent-encode it in the query string. http and https only, no credentials in the URL, no private, loopback or internal hosts, and the port must be one Cloudflare proxies (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 8880, 2052/2053/2082/2083/2086/2087/2095/2096). robots.txt is honoured for the user-agent token url2md.

example.description: The conversion result. The same metadata always travels in response headers as well, so a caller that asked for text/markdown still gets it: X-Url2md-Source (static | browser | pdf | origin-markdown | text), X-Url2md-Final-Url, X-Url2md-Title (percent-encoded), X-Url2md-Words, X-Url2md-Tokens-Estimate, X-Url2md-Ledger-Id (the ledger row for the settled payment), and X-Url2md-Upstream-Toll (USD paid to the origin when the page itself charged an x402 toll, absent otherwise). The x402 settlement receipt is in PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Errors are JSON with a stable error.code, and any error after a charge carries error.details.callerCharged with the ledger id.

blockSuspected.description: set when what came back looks like a bot challenge or block page rather than the page: the origin answered 200 and the call was charged, but the content is probably not what was asked for. Also sent as X-Url2md-Block-Suspected, and named in warnings[].

contentSignal.description: Upstream Content-Signal header, passed through untouched

finalUrl.description: the URL after redirects; also sent as X-Url2md-Final-Url

source.description: how the markdown was produced; also sent as X-Url2md-Source
